$comment: Hostile encampment, rebuilt on the Phase 9 kit (GDD "World art style guide"): the layout block is the single source for perimeter walls -- colliders and visuals both derive from it (defs/layout.go). Hand-authored colliders below are only the pieces the kit does not cover (the cover-post sphere). Contract: docs/GDD.md 'Phase 3 - NPC combat at an encampment' and 'Static colliders' for the authoring frame. Local frame: +x east, +y up as height ABOVE the terrain surface, +z north; yaw in degrees about +y, 0 = facing +z. SITE: chosen by sweeping the sphere against ALL 19 world features - spawn, the range zone, the 6 landmarks AND the 11 craters - for maximum clearance (142 m, against a 44 m flatten reach). The first site cleared landmarks but not craters and sat 39 m from one, levelling it: t9 read 10 of 11 craters confirmed in the field. The range zone made the same mistake against a landmark. Anything the terrain audit checks for has to be in the avoid set, not just the things you remembered.

colliders.$note: cover post — the sphere collider path

entities.$note: gunners hold the back, behind cover
grunts patrol the approach and close first

$props_comment: Camp dressing. VISUAL ONLY: props carry no collider and the server does not simulate them -- walk straight through one. They exist because a walled enclosure with five hostiles and bare ground in between reads as a test fixture rather than as somewhere anyone lives. Authored here rather than scattered client-side because the `colliders` message is world-space with no zone identity, so a client cannot tell this camp's walls from the range's and has nothing to place 'inside the camp' against. Same local frame as the colliders above: +x east, +y height above the surface, +z north, yaw degrees about +y. Kept clear of the five NPC spawns, the inner cover block at (3,2), the cover post at (-6,-5) and the west entrance gap at z in [-2,2] -- a barrel in the doorway is a barrel someone walks into and cannot push.
